neighbours.label: the ' in' of the idiom 'just in case'; 'just in time', locative 'just in' and plain 'in case' stay well below it
fire: The nurse wrote down the number, just in case.
Take a flashlight along on the hike just in case.
We booked a second hotel room just in case the flight was late.
Keep the old receipt for a month, just in case it breaks.
My mother always packs extra socks, just in case.
They hired a backup driver just in case someone fell ill.
I made a copy of the keys just in case you lose yours.
She stayed near the phone all evening, just in case.
quiet: The nurse wrote down the number in the chart.
Take a flashlight along on the hike in the dark.
We booked a second hotel room just in time for the flight.
Keep the old receipt in your wallet for a month.
My mother always packs extra socks just in winter.
They hired a backup driver in the middle of the season.
I made a copy of the keys just in time for your visit.
She stayed near the phone all evening in the kitchen.
